findings.decompiled: if not uint1(name): mem[128] = 256 * name.field_8 / _5 = _1 * bool(_1) + 128  |  signer = ecrecover(_24, v, r, s) ... _28 = mem[718 len 20] == owner and bool(owner)
findings.source: ERC20.sol DOMAIN_SEPARATOR: keccak256(bytes(name)); permit: address recoveredAddress = ecrecover(digest, v, r, s); require(recoveredAddress == owner && owner != address(0), 'ERC20:P:INVALID_SIGNATURE')
findings.issue: Small leftovers: 'x * bool(x)' is not folded to x, the short-string case reads the slot as '256 * name.field_8' (the slot without its length byte), and the recovered address is compared through its memory copy although it was just named signer.
findings.rule: x * bool(x) = x; '256 * (s >> 8)' is 's & ~0xff'; after 'signer = ecrecover(...)' whose result is copied to memory, a read of that copy (mem[718 len 20]) is address(signer).

notes: Unoptimised MapleToken (ERC20 with permit and module-based mint / burn), 23 functions, all reviewed in full; no loops in the source or the text. Transfers, allowances (with the infinite-allowance shortcut), mint / burn by modules, the governor-scheduled addModule / removeModule calls to globals (isValidScheduledCall / unscheduleCall with msg.data), DOMAIN_SEPARATOR and permit (deadline, malleability check, nonce, ecrecover) are all correct.
summary: A clean, faithful, loop-free text with only cosmetic simplifications left.
